ChatPatch.description:
Partial chat-metadata update: rename, star, and/or set the Chat override.
Absent field = unchanged; ``model=""`` clears the override back to inheriting.
ChatPatch.title: ChatPatch

ChatRowOut.description:
One drawer row. core.py list_chats normalises every field, so none is
optional: a missing title becomes "", an absent star becomes False.
ChatRowOut.title: ChatRowOut

CodexCodeRequest.description: Headless ChatGPT-subscription sign-in: a pasted auth code + its flow state.
CodexCodeRequest.title: CodexCodeRequest

CodexLoginUrlResponse.description:
POST /api/codex/login_url — the consent URL plus the flow ``state`` the
headless /submit fallback needs to quote back.
CodexLoginUrlResponse.title: CodexLoginUrlResponse

CodexStatusResponse.description:
GET /api/codex/status — codex_auth.status().

Every field but ``signed_in`` is None when signed out, and ``expires_at`` is
also None for a reused codex-cli session, whose expiry we do not read.
CodexStatusResponse.title: CodexStatusResponse

CodingAgentsResponse.description: GET /api/coding/agents — `error` appears only when a bridge lookup failed.
CodingAgentsResponse.title: CodingAgentsResponse

CodingCatalogResponse.description: GET /api/coding/{agent}/models — `reason` says WHY a catalog came back empty.
CodingCatalogResponse.title: CodingCatalogResponse

DepsStatusOut.description: Optional provider-library state for a config type (llm_configs.deps_status).
DepsStatusOut.title: DepsStatusOut

ErrorBody.description: Every error body in app.py has this shape: 105 of them return {"error": str}.
ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody

FsListingErrorOut.description:
GET /api/fs/list answers 200 with ok:false when the path is unreadable.

Declared as a separate member rather than optional fields on the success
model, so the two shapes stay distinguishable — the Literal on `ok`
discriminates them, which is what keeps the union from coercing one into the
other. Member ORDER mirrors FsListing in web/src/schemas/system.ts: the gate
matches anyOf branches by index.
FsListingErrorOut.title: FsListingErrorOut

FsMkdirRequest.description:
Create one subfolder inside a host directory the folder picker is viewing. Distinct
from `MkdirRequest`: that one writes into the Files space / a granted Folder, whereas
this runs BEFORE any Grant exists (you're choosing the folder to grant), so it is
host-scoped like its sibling `GET /api/fs/list`. `name` is a single component, not a
path.
FsMkdirRequest.title: FsMkdirRequest

FsMkdirResponse.description: POST /api/fs/mkdir — failures are non-2xx JSONResponse, not this body.
FsMkdirResponse.title: FsMkdirResponse

GoogleCredentialsErrorOut.description:
POST /api/google/credentials answers 200 with ok:false on a bad client
JSON — the upload form shows the parser's message inline rather than
treating it as a transport failure. Member ORDER mirrors OkOrError in
web/src/schemas/system.ts: the gate matches anyOf branches by index.
GoogleCredentialsErrorOut.title: GoogleCredentialsErrorOut

GoogleLoginUrlErrorOut.description:
No OAuth client configured, or the flow could not be built. Google answers
200 either way, so the failure branch rides the same body.
GoogleLoginUrlErrorOut.title: GoogleLoginUrlErrorOut

GoogleStatusResponse.description:
GET /api/google/status.

``libs_available`` is separate from ``signed_in`` on purpose: a token saved
without the optional [google] extra looks connected but can do nothing, and
``install_hint`` then carries the remedy (it is None when the libs are there).
GoogleStatusResponse.title: GoogleStatusResponse

HealthChannelOut.description:
One connection that defaults to this profile.

Field list read off the handler, not off the zod schema: settings.ts used to
declare a `token_present` the gateway never sent, and to omit the `connection`
and `name` it does send. The zod side was corrected to match this.
HealthChannelOut.title: HealthChannelOut

HealthCheckOut.description: One subsystem row. The mcp and channels rows carry extra detail.
HealthCheckOut.title: HealthCheckOut

HealthResponse.description:
GET /api/health and the gateway's own status().

The zero-profile stub answers {status, profiles}; a running install answers
gateway/core.py status(). Only `status` is common to both, so everything
else carries a default.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

IdentityRequest.description:
Identity answers collected in web onboarding (all optional). Seed the shared
universal "who the user is" doc, replacing the CLI first-chat interview.
IdentityRequest.title: IdentityRequest

IdentitySeededResponse.description:
POST /api/identity — seed-only.

`reason` says why a seed was skipped ("empty" or "exists") and is absent on
the branch that actually wrote, hence the default.
IdentitySeededResponse.title: IdentitySeededResponse

InquiryOut.description:
One open HITL inquiry. The last three fields resolve the asking run back
to its task so the strip can label and link the source.
InquiryOut.title: InquiryOut

LiveConfigOut.description: One named live (voice) configuration as the API exposes it.
LiveConfigOut.title: LiveConfigOut

LiveConfigRequest.description:
Create/update body for a named live (voice) configuration. A config's key is
its ``secret_id`` reference (a Secret in the secrets store). ``api_key`` is
DRAFT-TEST ONLY (a typed value is used directly, never persisted). ``id`` is
only read by the draft-test endpoint. ``voice`` is optional on save (defaults
to the provider's default voice; usually changed via the voice picker, not
this body).
LiveConfigRequest.title: LiveConfigRequest

LiveProviderOut.description: A voice provider's defaults, which seed the add-form and the templates.
LiveProviderOut.title: LiveProviderOut

LlmConfigListResponse.description:
GET /api/llm-configs. ``provider_deps`` covers every known type, not just
the configured ones — the "Add model" template grid reads it for types no
config uses yet.
LlmConfigListResponse.title: LlmConfigListResponse

LlmConfigOut.description:
One named LLM configuration as the API exposes it.

``signed_in`` is added only for ``type == "openai_subscription"`` — the live
ChatGPT sign-in state the chip needs without a second fetch — so it carries a
default and every route returning this model excludes unset fields.
LlmConfigOut.title: LlmConfigOut

LlmConfigRequest.description:
Create/update body for a named LLM configuration. A model's key is its
``secret_id`` reference (a Secret in the secrets store). ``api_key`` is
DRAFT-TEST ONLY: the /test endpoints use a typed value directly ("" tests as
if no Secret resolved); create/update ignore it. ``id`` is only read by the
draft-test endpoint (create/update take the id from the URL path).
LlmConfigRequest.title: LlmConfigRequest

LlmEnvOverrideOut.description:
The env pin banner payload: whichever of AG2ASSISTANT_LLM_PROVIDER /
AG2ASSISTANT_MODEL is set. Each key is present only when its variable is,
which is why both carry a default rather than being nullable-required.
LlmEnvOverrideOut.title: LlmEnvOverrideOut

MemoryDocResponse.description: GET /api/memory and GET /api/p/{pid}/memory — the raw document text.
MemoryDocResponse.title: MemoryDocResponse

MessageResponse.description: POST /api/p/{pid}/message — the assistant's reply and the chat it landed in.
MessageResponse.title: MessageResponse

MkdirRequest.description:
Create an empty Directory (ADR 0007). `path` is workspace-relative for the Files
space; for a Folder (ADR 0006, ticket 05) it is ABSOLUTE and stays inside a granted
Folder's subtree. `chat_id` scopes the read_write Grant resolution for a Folder
mkdir (ignored for a relative path).
MkdirRequest.title: MkdirRequest

MoveRequest.description:
Move/rename a file or Directory (ADR 0007). `from`/`to` are workspace-relative
for a Files-space move; for a Folder move (ADR 0006, ticket 04) both are ABSOLUTE
and must resolve under the SAME readable Folder root (no cross-Root move).
`chat_id` scopes the Grant resolution for a Folder move (ignored for a relative
move — the Files space is profile-sandboxed).
MoveRequest.title: MoveRequest

NewTaskEnvelopeResponse.description:
POST /api/p/{pid}/tasks — create_task answers with a freshly built row,
which has no ``runs`` key yet.
NewTaskEnvelopeResponse.title: NewTaskEnvelopeResponse

Ok.description: The bare acknowledgement a mutation route answers with.
Ok.title: Ok

PingResultResponse.description:
Both Test buttons on success. A failure is a 502 built by hand, so the
``ok: false`` branch never rides this model.
PingResultResponse.title: PingResultResponse

ProfileHealthResponse.description: GET /api/p/{pid}/health — `overall` rolls up the core signals only.
ProfileHealthResponse.title: ProfileHealthResponse

ProviderCatalogResponse.description:
GET /api/llm-configs/models — a provider's model catalog in the same
``{models, current, reason}`` envelope the ACP route uses, with
provider_catalog.py's own reasons. ``current`` is always empty here: a
provider names no model of its own.
ProviderCatalogResponse.title: ProviderCatalogResponse

RunDetailOut.description:
tasks_service.get_run stamps the owning task's name onto the run view —
the run header reads it.
RunDetailOut.title: RunDetailOut

RunListResponse.description:
GET /api/p/{pid}/tasks/{task_id}/runs — the history without task_name,
since the caller already knows the task.
RunListResponse.title: RunListResponse

RunOut.description:
One run, as tasks_service._run_view builds it.

``trigger`` is a bare str, not the Literal tasks/model.py pins it to: run
records outlive the version that wrote them, and no view reads the field, so
an older value must be rendered rather than rejected.
RunOut.title: RunOut

ScheduleOut.description:
A task's schedule, canonicalised to {kind, at, cron} by
tasks/model.py normalize_schedule.

``at`` and ``cron`` carry defaults rather than being required-nullable
because tasks/store.py create_task accepts a schedule dict unnormalised
(``schedule or manual_schedule()``), so a persisted row can be missing a key
that normalize_schedule would have filled. Both are declared: the schedule
editor reads them (components/task/ScheduleField.svelte), and a model that
did not declare them would silently drop them from the response.
ScheduleOut.title: ScheduleOut

SecretCreateRequest.description:
Create body for a Secret (named reusable API key — CONTEXT.md "Secrets").
``value`` is write-only: no endpoint ever returns it (views carry a last-4
hint). ``default`` requires a provider tag.
SecretCreateRequest.title: SecretCreateRequest

SecretOut.description:
One Secret's safe view.

``used_by`` is filled in only by ``GET /api/secrets``, which cross-references
the LLM and live config stores to drive the "used by N models" delete
confirm. The save routes answer with the store's bare view and say nothing
about references, so the field carries a default and those routes are
declared ``response_model_exclude_unset=True`` — shipping ``[]`` there would
claim "nothing uses this", which a rename or a rotate has not established.
SecretOut.title: SecretOut

SecretRefOut.description:
The trimmed Secret view embedded in an LLM or live config.

Deliberately narrower than the Secret's own view: a config row names the key
it points at, it does not restate the Secret's provider tag or Default flag.
SecretRefOut.title: SecretRefOut

SecretSavedResponse.description:
POST /api/secrets and POST /api/secrets/{sid}.

``ok`` is a Literal because the failure shapes (409 duplicate, 404 unknown,
400 bad input) are non-2xx bodies built by hand, not this model.
SecretSavedResponse.title: SecretSavedResponse

SecretUpdateRequest.description:
Partial update for a Secret — None leaves a field unchanged. Rotating
``value`` re-keys every model referencing this Secret.
SecretUpdateRequest.title: SecretUpdateRequest

SharedKeyOut.description:
The provider-wide env key summary both config views carry: which variable
holds the fallback key, whether it is set, and its last-4 hint.
SharedKeyOut.title: SharedKeyOut

StatusRowOut.description: One row of GET /api/status, which answers a bare array, not an envelope.
StatusRowOut.title: StatusRowOut

TaskEnvelopeResponse.description:
GET and PATCH /api/p/{pid}/tasks/{task_id} — both answer through
get_task, so both carry the run history.
TaskEnvelopeResponse.title: TaskEnvelopeResponse

TaskOut.description: One task row for the drawer — tasks_service._task_row.
TaskOut.title: TaskOut

TaskRulesResponse.description:
GET /api/p/{pid}/tasks/{task_id}/permissions — this task's own rules
only, never a union with the install-wide set.
TaskRulesResponse.title: TaskRulesResponse

TaskWithRunsOut.description: The same row plus its run history, as get_task returns it.
TaskWithRunsOut.title: TaskWithRunsOut

TranscriptMessageOut.description: One display turn: gateway/core.py writes {role, text} pairs.
TranscriptMessageOut.title: TranscriptMessageOut

TranscriptResponse.description:
GET /api/p/{pid}/chats/{chat_id}.

Carries the Chat's own model override ('' = it inherits) alongside the model
a message sent right now would run on, so the composer's switcher needs no
second call (ADR 0025).
TranscriptResponse.title: TranscriptResponse

UsageResponse.description: GET /api/p/{pid}/usage — today() plus the date it covers.
UsageResponse.title: UsageResponse

UsageRollupResponse.description: GET /api/usage — the install-wide sum carries neither date nor by_model.
UsageRollupResponse.title: UsageRollupResponse

UsageRowOut.description: One profile's row inside the install-wide roll-up.
UsageRowOut.title: UsageRowOut

UsageTotalsOut.description: One day's spend: usage.py _blank minus by_model.
UsageTotalsOut.title: UsageTotalsOut

get.description: The web UI is the Svelte client at /app.

post.description:
Begin a ChatGPT sign-in: return the consent URL for the UI to open, and
start a background loopback listener (localhost:1455) that completes the flow
when OpenAI redirects back. The UI polls GET /api/codex/status.

Headless fallback: exchange a manually pasted auth code for the flow's
pending PKCE verifier. Used when the loopback callback can't reach the box
(e.g. Docker/remote) — the user copies the ``code`` from the redirect URL.

get.description:
Read-only status of CLI coding agents (for the Settings "Coding agents"
card). In Docker with ``AG2ASSISTANT_ACP_BRIDGE`` set, reports the host
bridge and the agents it exposes; otherwise the locally-installed agents.
Never raises — an unreachable bridge is reported as ``connected: false``.

An ACP adapter's model catalog (agent: "claude" | "codex"), for the
Settings model picker: ``{models, current, reason}``. Lazy + guarded — a
missing adapter, bridge mode or a broken probe all read as an empty
catalog, but ``reason`` says WHICH, so the form explains itself instead of
silently degrading to a free-text field. ``?refresh=1`` skips the TTL cache.

Every configured instance of a platform, in creation order. An install that
already had bot tokens is migrated to one Connection per platform on this read.
A Connection's token(s) appear only as a set flag and a last-4 hint.

schema.title: Response List Connections Api Connections Get

post.description:
Register a Connection on ``platform`` with its token(s) and start it at once;
one that will not start still records its reason. Bad tokens or platform → 400.

delete.description:
Stop a Connection and forget it with its token(s), Peers, paired accounts,
pairing code, default-Profile entry and exposure records. Unknown → 404.

post.description:
Change a Connection's display name; its id, tokens and everything keyed by it
are untouched. Unknown Connection → 404, a blank name → 400.

Set the profile this Connection's conversations land in by default (or clear
it with profile:null). Takes effect on the next message — the adapter itself keeps
running either way. Unknown Connection → 404; unknown/archived pid → 400.

get.description:
This Connection's surfaces and every profile's reachability on each.
Default-allow, so a profile nobody has withdrawn reads true everywhere.

post.description:
Expose or withdraw one profile on one surface of this Connection; withdrawing
the default's last surface clears it. Unknown → 404, bad profile/surface → 400.

get.description: This Connection's group Peers and what each is pinned to. Unknown → 404.

post.description:
Re-point one of this Connection's groups at a profile exposed to its group
surface. Unknown Connection or group → 404; an unreachable profile → 400.

get.description:
Who may reach this one Connection, and its live one-time code (or null).
A grant here is no grant on another Connection of the same platform.

post.description: Allow an account on this Connection by numeric id or by handle.

Mint this Connection's one live code, replacing its earlier one and no
other's. The code works only on the Connection it was minted for.

delete.description: Withdraw one entry from this Connection alone. Nothing to withdraw → 404.

post.description:
Replace a Connection's token(s) and restart it on them, keeping its identity.
A replacement that will not start rolls back → 400; unknown → 404.

get.description: Every Folder with its path-exists badge and its Grants.

schema.title: Response Get Folders Api Folders Get

post.description:
Register a directory as a Folder. 400 for a non-directory; 409 with a
pointer when the resolved path is already registered (path-unique).

delete.description: Delete a Folder — always allowed; every Grant to it is revoked instantly.

post.description: Rename and/or repoint a Folder. 404 unknown; 409 path collision.

delete.description:
Revoke one Grant: (profile, task, chat) → mode. Empty chat_id+task_id = profile-scope.
404 when no such Grant exists.

post.description: Upsert one Grant: (profile, task, chat) → mode. Empty chat_id+task_id = profile-scope.

get.description:
List immediate subdirectories of a host path — drives the folder picker. The
gateway is local + single-user and `_origin_guard` blocks cross-origin, so this is
safe; dotfolders are hidden. Empty path starts at home.

schema.title: Response Fs List Api Fs List Get

post.description:
Create ONE subfolder inside the host directory the picker is viewing, so a
working folder can be made without leaving the app. Same trust model as
`fs_list` above (local + single-user, `_origin_guard` blocks cross-origin).

Returns the new folder's ABSOLUTE path — `make_dir` reports a root-relative one,
but the picker navigates by absolute path.
Save an uploaded OAuth client JSON (so users avoid the filesystem).

schema.title: Response Google Credentials Api Google Credentials Post

post.description:
Build a Google consent URL whose redirect returns to this gateway.

The user opens the URL (web button or a channel link). AG2ASSISTANT_PUBLIC_URL
overrides the redirect base when the gateway is reachable at a public URL
(so the round-trip can complete from another device).

schema.title: Response Google Login Url Api Google Login Url Post

get.description:
Process-level status: the first running runtime's gateway status, or a
zero-profile stub (fresh install, §3.5).

post.description:
Seed the universal "who the user is" doc from web-onboarding identity answers
(name/location/hours/style, all optional). Formats them with the SAME
`identity_document` helper the CLI interview uses, so both surfaces produce an
identical doc. Onboarding semantics: this only ever *seeds* — if the universal
store already holds a doc it is left untouched (returns ``seeded: false``), and
if every field is empty nothing is written (also ``seeded: false``). This is why
a web-onboarded user's first chat never triggers the in-chat interview: the
store is already seeded, so `needs_onboarding` is false.

get.description:
The install-wide named live configs, the active id, and the provider catalog
(default model/voice per provider) that seeds the add-form and templates.

post.description: Create a new named live configuration.

Probe a DRAFT live config as entered, WITHOUT saving. Registered before the
/{cid} routes so "test" isn't captured as an id. ``req.id`` lets a blank key
field fall back to that config's stored key; a typed key is used directly.

delete.description:
Delete a live config (404 if unknown). Deleting the active one moves active to
the next remaining config (or none — legacy fallback). Referenced Secrets are
independent and untouched.

post.description: Update an existing named live configuration (404 if unknown).
Models-list key probe against a SAVED live config. 404 if unknown.
Make ``cid`` the active live configuration (404 if unknown).

get.description:
The install-wide named LLM configs, the active id, and any env override that
pins provider/model over them (drives the 'pinned by env' UI banner).

post.description: Create a new named LLM configuration.

get.description:
A provider's model catalog in the ACP route's ``{models, current, reason}``
envelope, named by type, endpoint and ``secret_id`` — no key material (ADR
0024). ``?refresh=1`` forbids the HTTP cache; there is no other.

post.description:
Test a DRAFT configuration exactly as entered in the editor, WITHOUT saving.
Registered before the /{cid} routes so the literal "test" segment isn't
captured as an id. ``req.id`` (when editing an existing config) lets a blank
key field fall back to that config's stored key, matching what a save would
produce; a typed ``api_key`` is used directly and never persisted.

delete.description:
Delete a config (404 if unknown). Deleting the active one moves active to the
next remaining config (or none — flat defaults). Reloads every runtime so the
new active takes effect (referenced Secrets are independent and untouched).

post.description: Update an existing named LLM configuration (404 if unknown).

Real PONG round-trip against a SAVED config, exercising the exact runtime
key-resolution path. 404 if unknown; result shape per ``_ping_entry``.
Make ``cid`` the active configuration and reload every runtime (404 unknown).

get.description:
Read the shared universal "who the user is" document (identity facts injected
into EVERY profile's context). Mirrors the per-profile GET /api/p/{pid}/memory.

post.description:
Replace the shared universal document (a user edit from any profile's Settings →
Memory). Read fresh per turn, so all profiles' agents pick it up next turn.
Mark first-run onboarding completed/dismissed (install-level, in the registry).

get.description: List persisted, resumable conversations (newest first).

delete.description: Permanently delete a chat (transcript + full event log). Irreversible.

get.description:
The display transcript for a chat, plus its Chat override and the model it
would run on right now (so the composer's switcher needs no second call).

patch.description:
Rename, star, and/or set the Chat override. 400 on an empty patch, 404 on
unknown chat.

get.description:
List a file tree, branching on ``os.path.isabs`` (the sole discriminator).

With no ``path`` (or a relative one) — the profile's whole Files space: files
plus every Directory (so the tree can show empty Directories the files-only
listing omits). Shared read+write; agent writes and user uploads land here
alike (ADR 0007).

With an ABSOLUTE ``path`` — ONE Directory level inside a granted **Folder** (a
directory outside the Root), authorized through the one resolver (``read``
suffices), scoped to the open Thread (``chat_id``, plus the task decoded from it
so a Task page/run sees its task-scope Folders — ADR 0006/0013), with the usual
noise Directories pruned. The tree lazy-expands one level per call. A
denied/missing path is a 404 — the same shape either branch.

The preview rail's "Mentioned in N threads" backlink (ADR 0014): the
current profile's Threads (Chats + Task Runs) whose transcript mentions the
previewed file, newest-first. ``path`` is the previewed file's path (relative
= Files-space, absolute = Folder); its OR-set of forms (absolute + workspace-
relative) is loose-substring-scanned over each stream's transcript + event
log. Read-only over this profile's own store — no auth/grant check beyond the
profile boundary. ``chat_id`` is accepted for signature parity with the other
``/files`` routes but not needed (the scan is profile-wide).

schema.title: Response File Mentions Api P  Pid  Files Mentions Get

post.description:
Create an empty Directory. 409 if it already exists (no clobber), 400 on a
traversal escape / empty path. A RELATIVE `path` lands in the Files-space
sandbox (unchanged). An ABSOLUTE `path` creates a Folder Directory: it
authorizes through the one resolver requiring `read_write` (a `read`-only Folder
is `403`), scoped to the open Thread (`chat_id` + the task decoded from it),
confined to that Folder's subtree (ticket 05).

Move/rename a file or Directory. 409 if the destination already exists
(never overwrites, ADR 0007), 404 if the source is missing, 400 on a
traversal escape.

A RELATIVE ``from`` moves within the Files-space sandbox (unchanged). An
ABSOLUTE ``from`` is a Folder move: it authorizes through the one resolver
requiring ``read_write`` (a ``read``-only Folder is ``403``), scoped to
``chat_id``, and is confined to the source's own readable Folder root — so a
``to`` that resolves outside it (another root, the Files space, or a relative
target) is rejected ``400`` (no cross-Root move, ticket 04).

delete.description:
Delete a file — or a Directory and everything in it, recursively (ADR
0007). A RELATIVE ``path`` is sandboxed to the Files-space root (unchanged). An
ABSOLUTE ``path`` is a Folder file/Directory: it authorizes through the one
resolver requiring ``read_write`` (a ``read``-only Folder is ``403``), scoped
to ``chat_id``, and the delete is confined to that Folder's own subtree
(emptied parents pruned up to — never including — the Folder root, ticket 04).

get.description:
Serve one file (view inline or download). A RELATIVE ``path`` is a
Files-space file, sandboxed to the workspace root (ADR 0007). An ABSOLUTE
``path`` is a Folder file (a file inside a granted Folder outside the Root):
authorized through the one resolver (``read`` suffices), scoped to the open
Thread's ``chat_id`` (ADR 0006/0013). Either way carries an ``ETag``
content-version token (ADR 0011) an in-place ``PUT`` echoes back as
``If-Match``. A denied/missing path is a 404 — the same shape either branch.
The response also carries ``X-File-Mode`` (``read``|``read_write``) — the
effective Grant mode — so the client gates its edit/rename/delete affordances
off the same server truth a mutation is enforced against (ticket 04).

put.description:
Overwrite an existing file's contents in place from the request body
(UTF-8), using ``If-Match`` as the base ETag (ADR 0011). ``200`` + the new
``ETag`` on success, ``404`` if the path is missing, ``409`` if ``If-Match``
is stale, ``400`` on a traversal/invalid path; omitting ``If-Match`` forces
past the compare.

A RELATIVE ``path`` writes in the Files-space sandbox (unchanged). An ABSOLUTE
``path`` is a Folder file: it authorizes through the one resolver requiring
``read_write`` (a ``read``-only Folder file is ``403``), scoped to the open
Thread's ``chat_id``, and the write is confined to that Folder's own subtree
(ticket 04).

get.description:
The ``@``-picker's corpus search: a bounded, ranked list of files matching
`q` across the profile's Files space **and** every Folder this profile∪task∪chat
can read, each with an ABSOLUTE `path` the agent's ``read_file`` can open.
Ranked filename-first; a blank/no-match query yields an empty list, not an
error. Honors the same ``mode_for`` resolution the agent's reads use, so a
denied file is never surfaced (ADR 0006/0012).

schema.title: Response Search Workspace Files Api P  Pid  Files Search Get

post.description:
Upload one or more files into `dir` (root when empty), auto-suffixing name
clashes so nothing is overwritten (ADR 0007). A RELATIVE `dir` targets the
Files-space sandbox (unchanged). An ABSOLUTE `dir` targets a Folder Directory:
it authorizes through the one resolver requiring `read_write` (a `read`-only
Folder is `403`), scoped to the open Thread (`chat_id` + the task decoded from
it), with the upload confined to that Folder's subtree (ticket 05). A `dir` that
escapes its root is rejected `400`.

get.description:
The Folder roots browsable in the open Thread — the tree's Thread-scoped
Folder section (ADR 0013). Each root: ``{id, name, path (absolute), mode,
exists}``, resolved through the same ``mode_for`` truth the ``@``-picker and the
agent's reads share, scoped by ``chat_id`` plus the task decoded from it (a Task
page carries ``task:{id}``, a run thread ``task-run:{run_id}``), so the open
Task/run's task-scope Folders surface, not just profile grants (absent scope →
profile-level grants only). A missing-path Folder is included as a badged,
repointable root (``exists: false``), never an error.

schema.title: Response List Folder Roots Api P  Pid  Folders Roots Get

get.description:
Cheap, at-a-glance health of this profile's subsystems — the source for
the UI's status dot. Presence/liveness signals ONLY: no MCP subprocess
spawns, no provider pings, so it's cheap enough to poll on a short cycle.
MCP servers are listed (config only) and probed on demand by the client via
``/settings/mcp/{name}/health``.

``overall`` rolls up the *core* signals: ``down`` if the agent isn't alive or
the configured provider has no key (the agent can't run); ``warn`` if a
channel bound to this profile failed to start; else ``ok``. Google and the
scheduler are informational and never move ``overall``.

Per-profile activity for badges: busy = agent alive, running_tasks = count

Install-wide token/cost roll-up across ALL running profiles (for the HUD's
"all profiles" total). ``profiles`` is one ``usage_today()`` snapshot per
running runtime (with its ``pid``/``name``); ``total`` sums the numeric fields.

``total.priced`` is true only when EVERY contributing profile is priced — an
unpriced profile means its tokens carry no cost, so the summed ``cost`` is an
underestimate and the flag says so (matching the per-profile flag semantics and
the HUD's "no price set" fallback). Archived profiles aren't running, so they're
naturally excluded. Zero profiles → empty list + a zeroed total.
